correctness.rationale: The oriented chain-map proof is algebraically complete for every n>=2 and 1<=r<=n-1: a fixed simplex has e transpose pairs and d diagonal singleton orbits, contributing (-1)^(d+e+1); summing permitted diagonal choices gives (1-1)^u and annihilates every graph having degree below the cap. Precisely the labeled simple r-regular graphs remain, each with nr/2 edges. Hopf trace on the augmented chain complex justifies the empty-face minus sign. The Betti lower bound follows from trace absolute values; the two-regular EGF from labeled cycle components; the extremal orientation uses explicitly Singh Theorem 1.2 and the dimension parity. The standalone checker directly enumerates oriented fixed faces for every cap n=2..4 and independently enumerates regular graphs, with all six cases in agreement; an independent cycle recursion matches simple-graph counts to n=6. The computations are cross-checks only. No unproved claim about homology concentration away from r=n-1 is made.

originality.rationale: No inspected primary theorem or relevant indexed public finding supplies the factor-swapping reduced Lefschetz character for all n and degree caps. Singh supplies the nonequivariant extremal homotopy sphere, and Reiner–Roberts supplies the rational representation under the normal subgroup of separate row/column relabelings; neither specifies the action of the extra transpose generator. The exact small M2(K4,4) paper likewise establishes only a nonequivariant wedge of spheres. Closest similarly equivariant results concern a mathematically distinct graph Morse complex or matching complexes of rectangular grids. The general regular-graph cancellation identity therefore adds information not implied by the compared conclusions. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment, not proof of globally unique publication.

value.rationale: This natural bipartite factor-interchange symmetry is missing from standard nonequivariant higher matching homotopy results and from the independently acting row/column representation. The all-n, all-r formula links a topological homology character to labeled r-regular graph enumeration (including the nontrivial cycle-decomposition EGF for r=2), gives unconditional lower bounds on unknown total Betti numbers, and determines a previously unspecified sign on an infinite family of integral homotopy spheres. The precise invariant is independently motivated by the full automorphism group and potentially useful even when graded homology is not known. It is not an arbitrary finite census, cosmetic corollary, or routine renaming of a published theorem.
